newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips back, Sept falters above 1,060.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips back, Sept falters above 1,060.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures slipped back on trade selling to end Thursday midsession broadly lower after second-month September failed to hold above 1,060 stg.
The strong pound sterling also did not help the situation and September eventually finished the morning trade eight stg lower at 1,049, well above its immediate support at just beneath 1,045.
September hit an intraday high of 1,061 stg a tonne, the highest since the market tumbled to the July 3 low of 1,000 and ended a dazzling rally.
"Trade sellers emerged after it became apparent that September won't break the 1,060 level," said one trader.
Midday volume was fairly modest at 4,685 lots, made up mostly of crosses and switches.
Sterling recovered back above 2.96 German marks after shedding a pfenning on news Bank of England raised official interest rates by 25 basis points to 6.75 percent.
At 1108 GMT, the pound was 2.9540/50 marks, compared to 2.9640 pre-rate announcement and 2.9671/81 in late European trading on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, sterling eclipsed Tuesday's six-year high to reach a fresh peak at 2.9760 marks.
A strong sterling deters many European buyers but attracts selling from the origins.
